resource.name: aws_s3_object
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_s3_object` Terraform resource enables the creation and management of individual objects within an Amazon S3 bucket, supporting file uploads, metadata configuration, and access control settings. Common use cases include storing application assets, backups, or static website files, as well as integrating with workflows for data processing or content delivery. Users can configure object properties such as versioning, encryption, caching headers, and lifecycle rules to optimize storage, security, and performance.

examples.title: Uploading a file to a bucket
examples.code:
resource "aws_s3_object" "object" {
  bucket = "your_bucket_name"
  key    = "new_object_key"
  source = "path/to/file"

  # The filemd5() function is available in Terraform 0.11.12 and later
  # For Terraform 0.11.11 and earlier, use the md5() function and the file() function:
  # etag = "${md5(file("path/to/file"))}"
  etag = filemd5("path/to/file")
}
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates how to upload a file to an S3 bucket using the `aws_s3_object` resource, specifying the bucket name, object key, and file path. Highlights the use of the `filemd5()` function to set the `etag` for file integrity verification."

examples.title: Encrypting with KMS Key
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates how to configure an `aws_s3_object` resource with server-side encryption using a custom AWS KMS key (`kms_key_id`) for enhanced data security. Includes setup of an S3 bucket, private ACL, and integration with a KMS key to encrypt an uploaded object."

examples.title: Server Side Encryption with S3 Default Master Key
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure server-side encryption for an S3 object using the default AWS KMS master key (`aws:kms`) with the `server_side_encryption` argument. It also illustrates creating an S3 bucket, setting its ACL to private, and uploading an object with encryption enabled, providing a secure storage solution for sensitive data.

examples.title: Server Side Encryption with AWS-Managed Key
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an `aws_s3_object` resource with server-side encryption using the AWS-managed AES256 key. It illustrates uploading an object to an S3 bucket with private ACL settings, specifying the `server_side_encryption` argument to ensure data is encrypted at rest.

examples.title: S3 Object Lock
examples.llm_summary: This Terraform example demonstrates how to configure an `aws_s3_object` with Object Lock features, including legal hold (`object_lock_legal_hold_status`), governance mode (`object_lock_mode`), and a retention date (`object_lock_retain_until_date`). It also showcases dependencies on bucket versioning and highlights advanced S3 bucket settings like enabling Object Lock and private ACLs for secure and compliant data management.

examples.title: Ignoring Provider default_tags
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure the `aws_s3_object` resource to override the default provider `default_tags` configuration, ensuring custom tags are applied to the S3 object without inheriting default tags. It illustrates the use of the `override_provider` block and the `tags` argument for precise tag management.

arguments.name: acl
arguments.description: (Optional) Canned ACL to apply. Valid values are `private`, `public-read`, `public-read-write`, `aws-exec-read`, `authenticated-read`, `bucket-owner-read`, and `bucket-owner-full-control`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `acl` argument in the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to define the access control list (ACL) for the S3 object, specifying its permissions and visibility. By setting this argument, users can control who can read, write, or manage the object, aligning with common goals like securing data, enabling public access, or delegating permissions to authenticated users or bucket owners.

arguments.name: bucket
arguments.description: (Required) Name of the bucket to put the file in. Alternatively, an S3 access point ARN can be specified.
arguments.llm_summary: The `bucket` argument specifies the target S3 bucket where the object will be stored, allowing users to define the storage location by providing the bucket's name or an S3 access point ARN. This is a required parameter that directly determines the destination for the uploaded file, aligning with user goals of managing object storage and organizing data within AWS S3.

arguments.name: bucket_key_enabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether or not to use Amazon S3 Bucket Keys for SSE-KMS.
arguments.llm_summary: The `bucket_key_enabled` argument for the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to control whether Amazon S3 Bucket Keys are used for server-side encryption with AWS KMS (SSE-KMS). Enabling this feature optimizes encryption performance and reduces costs by minimizing the number of KMS requests, making it ideal for users prioritizing efficient encryption management for S3 objects.

arguments.name: cache_control
arguments.description: (Optional) Caching behavior along the request/reply chain Read w3c cache_control for further details.
arguments.llm_summary: The `cache_control` argument for the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to define HTTP caching behavior for the object, specifying directives that control how browsers and intermediate caches handle requests and responses. By setting this argument, users can optimize content delivery, manage cache expiration, and improve performance for frequently accessed objects.

arguments.name: checksum_algorithm
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicates the algorithm used to create the checksum for the object. If a value is specified and the object is encrypted with KMS, you must have permission to use the `kms:Decrypt` action. Valid values: `CRC32`, `CRC32C`, `CRC64NVME`, `SHA1`, `SHA256`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `checksum_algorithm` argument for the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to specify the algorithm used to generate a checksum for the uploaded object, ensuring data integrity during storage or transfer. Setting this argument enables validation of the object's content using algorithms like `CRC32`, `SHA256`, or others, and may require additional permissions if the object is encrypted with KMS.

arguments.name: content
arguments.description: (Optional, conflicts with `source` and `content_base64`) Literal string value to use as the object content, which will be uploaded as UTF-8-encoded text.
arguments.llm_summary: The `content` argument in the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to directly specify the literal UTF-8-encoded text that will be uploaded as the object's content in an S3 bucket. This enables users to define the object's data inline, simplifying scenarios where the content is small, static, or generated dynamically within the Terraform configuration, without relying on external files or encoded sources.

arguments.name: content_base64
arguments.description: (Optional, conflicts with `source` and `content`) Base64-encoded data that will be decoded and uploaded as raw bytes for the object content. This allows safely uploading non-UTF8 binary data, but is recommended only for small content such as the result of the `gzipbase64` function with small text strings. For larger objects, use `source` to stream the content from a disk file.
arguments.llm_summary: The `content_base64` argument for the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to upload Base64-encoded binary data as the object's content, enabling the safe handling of non-UTF8 or small binary files directly within Terraform. This is ideal for scenarios where users need to define small, encoded object content without relying on external file sources, but it is recommended to use `source` for larger files to optimize performance and resource management.

arguments.name: content_disposition
arguments.description: (Optional) Presentational information for the object. Read w3c content_disposition for further information.
arguments.llm_summary: The `content_disposition` argument for the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to define how the object should be presented or handled when accessed, such as specifying if it should be displayed inline or downloaded as an attachment. This configuration is commonly used to control the behavior of file downloads or browser rendering, aligning with user goals like customizing content delivery and enhancing user experience.

arguments.name: content_encoding
arguments.description: (Optional) Content encodings that have been applied to the object and thus what decoding mechanisms must be applied to obtain the media-type referenced by the Content-Type header field. Read w3c content encoding for further information.
arguments.llm_summary: The `content_encoding` argument for the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to specify the encoding transformations applied to the object's data, such as `gzip` or `deflate`. This configuration informs clients how to decode the object to access its original media type, enabling efficient data transfer and compatibility with specific applications or browsers.

arguments.name: content_language
arguments.description: (Optional) Language the content is in e.g., en-US or en-GB.
arguments.llm_summary: The `content_language` argument for the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to specify the language of the object's content, such as `en-US` or `en-GB`, by setting the `Content-Language` metadata header. This helps define language-specific context for the object, which can be useful for applications that rely on localization or need to communicate language preferences to downstream systems or clients.

arguments.name: content_type
arguments.description: (Optional) Standard MIME type describing the format of the object data, e.g., application/octet-stream. All Valid MIME Types are valid for this input.
arguments.llm_summary: The `content_type` argument for the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to specify the MIME type of the object's data, defining its format and enabling proper handling by applications or browsers (e.g., `application/json`, `image/png`). Setting this argument ensures accurate content identification, which is critical for use cases like serving web assets, configuring API responses, or managing file compatibility in S3.

arguments.name: etag
arguments.description: (Optional) Triggers updates when the value changes. The only meaningful value is `filemd5("path/to/file")` (Terraform 0.11.12 or later) or `${md5(file("path/to/file"))}` (Terraform 0.11.11 or earlier). This attribute is not compatible with KMS encryption, `kms_key_id` or `server_side_encryption = "aws:kms"`, also if an object is larger than 16 MB, the AWS Management Console will upload or copy that object as a Multipart Upload, and therefore the ETag will not be an MD5 digest (see `source_hash` instead).
arguments.llm_summary: The `etag` argument in the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to define a checksum value (typically an MD5 hash) to trigger updates when the file content changes. It is primarily used for ensuring file integrity and detecting changes in the source file, but it is incompatible with KMS encryption and multipart uploads for objects larger than 16 MB, making it ideal for smaller, non-encrypted files.

arguments.name: force_destroy
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether to allow the object to be deleted by removing any legal hold on any object version. Default is `false`. This value should be set to `true` only if the bucket has S3 object lock enabled.
arguments.llm_summary: The `force_destroy` argument for the `aws_s3_object` resource controls whether an S3 object can be forcibly deleted by overriding any legal hold on its versions, which is particularly relevant when S3 Object Lock is enabled. Setting this to `true` allows users to bypass retention constraints for deletion, supporting scenarios where strict cleanup or resource removal is required.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument for the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to specify a unique identifier for the S3 object, typically used to reference or manage the object programmatically within Terraform configurations. While optional, setting this argument can help users track and interact with the object in workflows or integrations that require explicit identification.

arguments.name: key
arguments.description: (Required) Name of the object once it is in the bucket. The following arguments are optional:
arguments.llm_summary: The `key` argument specifies the unique name or path for the object within the S3 bucket, effectively defining its location and identifier. Setting this argument allows users to organize and retrieve objects in the bucket, supporting common goals like structuring data hierarchies or ensuring predictable access paths for applications.

arguments.name: kms_key_id
arguments.description: (Optional) ARN of the KMS Key to use for object encryption. If the S3 Bucket has server-side encryption enabled, that value will automatically be used. If referencing the `aws_kms_key` resource, use the `arn` attribute. If referencing the `aws_kms_alias` data source or resource, use the `target_key_arn` attribute. Terraform will only perform drift detection if a configuration value is provided.
arguments.llm_summary: The `kms_key_id` argument allows users to specify the ARN of a KMS key for encrypting the S3 object, enabling fine-grained control over server-side encryption. By setting this argument, users can override the default encryption behavior of the S3 bucket and ensure the object is encrypted using a specific KMS key, aligning with security and compliance requirements.

arguments.name: metadata
arguments.description: (Optional) Map of keys/values to provision metadata (will be automatically prefixed by `x-amz-meta-`, note that only lowercase label are currently supported by the AWS Go API).
arguments.llm_summary: The `metadata` argument for the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to define custom key-value pairs as metadata for the S3 object, which are automatically prefixed with `x-amz-meta-`. This enables users to attach additional contextual information, such as environment tags, cache control hints, or application-specific data, to the object for retrieval or processing during downstream workflows.

arguments.name: object_lock_legal_hold_status
arguments.description: (Optional) Legal hold status that you want to apply to the specified object. Valid values are `ON` and `OFF`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `object_lock_legal_hold_status` argument for the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to specify the legal hold status of an S3 object, controlling whether the object is protected from deletion or modification due to compliance requirements. By setting this argument to `ON` or `OFF`, users can enforce or release legal holds, supporting regulatory or governance goals such as data retention policies.

arguments.name: object_lock_mode
arguments.description: (Optional) Object lock retention mode that you want to apply to this object. Valid values are `GOVERNANCE` and `COMPLIANCE`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `object_lock_mode` argument for the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to specify the retention mode for the object, enabling governance or compliance controls to prevent accidental or unauthorized modifications or deletions. By setting this argument to `GOVERNANCE` or `COMPLIANCE`, users can enforce stricter data protection policies, aligning with regulatory or organizational requirements for data retention and security.

arguments.name: object_lock_retain_until_date
arguments.description: (Optional) Date and time, in RFC3339 format, when this object's object lock will expire.
arguments.llm_summary: The `object_lock_retain_until_date` argument for the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to specify the expiration date and time (in RFC3339 format) for the object's retention period under S3 Object Lock. By setting this argument, users can enforce write protection on the object until the specified date, supporting compliance and data governance goals such as preventing accidental deletion or modification during a defined retention window.

arguments.name: server_side_encryption
arguments.description: (Optional) Server-side encryption of the object in S3. Valid values are "`AES256`" and "`aws:kms`".
arguments.llm_summary: The `server_side_encryption` argument for the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to specify the encryption mechanism applied to the object at rest in S3, enhancing data security and compliance. By setting this argument to either `AES256` or `aws:kms`, users can configure server-side encryption to protect sensitive data, aligning with common goals like securing storage and meeting regulatory requirements.

arguments.name: source
arguments.description: (Optional, conflicts with `content` and `content_base64`) Path to a file that will be read and uploaded as raw bytes for the object content.
arguments.llm_summary: The `source` argument in the `aws_s3_object` resource specifies the local file path to upload as the object's raw content in the S3 bucket. This allows users to define the source of the object's data directly from a file, enabling efficient content management and automation for file-based workflows, such as backups or static asset deployments.

arguments.name: source_hash
arguments.description: (Optional) Triggers updates like `etag` but useful to address `etag` encryption limitations. Set using `filemd5("path/to/source")` (Terraform 0.11.12 or later). (The value is only stored in state and not saved by AWS.)
arguments.llm_summary: The `source_hash` argument in the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to define a hash value (e.g., MD5) of the source file to track changes and trigger updates to the S3 object, even when `etag` cannot be reliably used due to encryption or other limitations. This ensures accurate state management and update detection without relying on AWS-stored metadata, supporting use cases like versioning or ensuring file integrity.

arguments.name: storage_class
arguments.description: (Optional) Storage Class for the object. Defaults to "`STANDARD`".
arguments.llm_summary: The `storage_class` argument for the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to specify the storage tier for the S3 object, such as `STANDARD`, `REDUCED_REDUNDANCY`, or `GLACIER`, optimizing cost and performance based on access patterns and retention needs. By configuring this, users can align object storage with their application's requirements, such as long-term archival, infrequent access, or high-availability use cases.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) Map of tags to assign to the object. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument for the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to assign key-value metadata to the S3 object, enabling categorization, organization, and resource management (e.g., for cost allocation, environment labeling, or automation workflows). When specified, these tags can override provider-level default tags, offering granular control over object-specific tagging.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument for the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags inherited from both user-defined tags and provider-level default tags. This enables efficient organization, categorization, and cost allocation for the S3 object, aligning with common tagging strategies for resource management and governance in AWS.

arguments.name: website_redirect
arguments.description: (Optional) Target URL for website redirect. If no content is provided through source, content or content_base64, then the object will be empty. Terraform ignores all leading /s in the object's key and treats multiple /s in the rest of the object's key as a single /, so values of /index.html and index.html correspond to the same S3 object as do first//second///third// and first/second/third/.
arguments.llm_summary: The `website_redirect` argument in the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to specify a target URL for redirecting requests made to the S3 object, enabling website redirection functionality. This is typically used to configure custom routing behavior for web applications or static websites hosted on S3, ensuring that requests to the object are forwarded to the defined URL.

blocks.name: override_provider
blocks.description: (Optional) Override provider-level configuration options. See Override Provider below for more details.

blocks.name: default_tags

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) Map of tags to assign to the object. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level.
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument for the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to define a custom map of key-value pairs to assign metadata tags to the S3 object, enabling resource categorization, organization, or tracking (e.g., environment, cost center, or project identifiers). When used alongside the provider-level `default_tags` configuration, this argument provides granular control by overriding matching default tags, ensuring flexibility in tag management for specific objects.

blocks.llm_summary: The `default_tags` configuration block within the `override_provider` context for the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to override the default tagging behavior defined at the provider level. This block enables fine-grained control over resource tagging by specifying custom key-value pairs, ensuring consistent metadata management and alignment with organizational tagging policies for the specific S3 object.

The `override_provider` block in the `aws_s3_object` resource allows users to customize provider-level configurations for the resource, enabling granular control over how the resource interacts with the AWS provider. This block is typically used to override default provider settings, such as credentials, regions, or endpoints, ensuring compatibility with specific environments or use cases, such as multi-account setups or custom AWS configurations.

attributes.name: checksum_crc32
attributes.description: The base64-encoded, 32-bit CRC32 checksum of the object.

attributes.name: checksum_crc32c
attributes.description: The base64-encoded, 32-bit CRC32C checksum of the object.

attributes.name: checksum_crc64nvme
attributes.description: The base64-encoded, 64-bit CRC64NVME checksum of the object.

attributes.name: checksum_sha1
attributes.description: The base64-encoded, 160-bit SHA-1 digest of the object.

attributes.name: checksum_sha256
attributes.description: The base64-encoded, 256-bit SHA-256 digest of the object.

attributes.name: version_id
attributes.description: Unique version ID value for the object, if bucket versioning is enabled.
